inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text:
Look, we need to talk about the absolute gaslighting coming from the political establishment, starting right at the top with Taoiseach Micheál Martin down in Limerick this past week. He’s trying to spin a narrative that housing tenancies have actually increased, completely turning a blind eye to the grim reality facing vulnerable workers and families on the ground. It’s painfully clear that the entire system is rigged to protect capital and property owners at the direct expense of human rights, and yet they still have the audacity to point fingers at basic protections. 

We saw this structural failure play out clearly when the Government introduced new rules on March 1 forcing landlords to provide rigid six-year leases. The apologists for the status quo want to cry about state meddling, but let's be honest—the real crisis is the relentless commodification of housing and the deep systemic inequality that leaves tenants entirely at the mercy of landlords. Instead of any real push for systemic housing justice, we are stuck with a rigged system where property owners wield disproportionate power. That power imbalance is leading directly to a surge in eviction notices and homelessness, driving the numbers of people trapped in emergency accommodation nationally up yet again. 

When you commodify a fundamental human right like shelter just to safeguard the interests of property, the social fabric inevitably frays, leaving working-class families to suffer under unchecked corporate and landlord greed. It is long past time to stop propping up this structural inequality. We need to demand real institutional reform, guaranteed housing rights, and robust protections for the vulnerable that put human lives way above the profit margins of landlords.
